card: This PR adds functional tests in tool_bitcoin.py to ensure the Windows bitcoin wrapper process preserves child exit codes and handles launch failures properly. It uses cmd.exe as a mock child to verify that exit codes 0, 1, and -1 are passed through without polluting stdout or stderr, guarding against Windows CRT quirks where an exit code of -1 was conflated with a spawn failure. It also checks that missing child binaries return exit code 1 with an error on stderr. It follows up on runtime wrapper fixes merged in #36105.
changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to test logic; commit history includes launch failure test coverage carried from the earlier iteration.
evidence: Commit 7395505c2f notes this test 'detects a bug that was present in the original implementation of the earlier commit "Fix ExecVp on Windows to wait for child process"'
PR description confirms that 'Against the old launcher this test fails at not(1 == 4294967295)'
problem: Without regression tests on Windows, flaws in wrapper process launching and exit code forwarding can go undetected. Specifically, Windows CRT spawn functions like _spawnvp(_P_WAIT) historically conflated a child exit status of -1 with process execution failure, causing the wrapper to emit a startup error and exit with code 1 instead of forwarding -1.

risk.why: A bug in this functional test would only cause false test failures or flakes on Windows CI.

summary: Adds functional tests to tool_bitcoin.py verifying that the Windows bitcoin wrapper process correctly preserves child exit statuses and reports launch failures. It mocks a child process using cmd.exe to check that exit codes 0, 1, and -1 are passed through without unexpected standard stream output, and tests that failure to find or launch the child executable reports an execvp failure on stderr with exit code 1.
